reading.title: Learning a New Language
reading.text: Dilnoza is fifteen, and she wants to speak English fluently. Uzbek is her mother tongue, and she also speaks Russian quite well. Last summer she joined a language course at a small school in her city. At first the language barrier was a problem, because her teacher, Mr Brown, spoke only English. However, his body language and his pictures helped her to understand. Now she reads English books every evening to improve her language. She hopes to study abroad one day.

listening.script: Anna: Hi, Tom! Are you taking a language course this term? Tom: Yes, I'm learning Italian. My grandmother's first language is Italian, but my parents never taught me. Anna: That's a shame! How is the course? Tom: It's great. We have lessons twice a week, and I'm improving my language skills quickly. Anna: Is it difficult? Tom: Pronunciation is the hardest part for me. I'm going to Rome in July, so I want to be ready.

reading.title: A Long Train Journey
reading.text: Last week I took a train to Samarkand. I sat next to an old man, and at first we did not speak. Then I tried to make conversation and asked him about the weather. He smiled, and soon we were having a friendly conversation about his life. He told me stories about the old days in the city. A woman behind us overheard our conversation and joined in. Time passed quickly, and the long journey did not feel boring. When we arrived, I said goodbye to my new friends.

reading.title: The Class Discussion
reading.text: On Monday our teacher, Ms Karimova, opened a discussion about mobile phones at school. She asked, "Should students use phones in lessons?" It soon became a heated discussion. Some students said phones are useful for finding information. Others said they only make us lose focus. Ms Karimova asked a quiet boy to join in the discussion, and he gave a very good idea. In the end, after much discussion, we agreed that phones can be used only for learning. The matter is still under discussion with the headmaster.

reading.title: My First Speech
reading.text: Last month our English teacher organised a speech contest. I was very nervous, but I decided to take part. I wrote my speech about my grandfather's village, and I practised it every evening. On the day of the contest, I walked on to the stage and gave my speech in front of a hundred people. My hands were shaking, but nobody noticed. When I finished, everyone clapped. I did not win first prize, but my teacher said it was a brave speech. Now I want to make another one.

reading.title: The School Rumour
reading.text: Last week a rumour spread around our school. People said that our favourite teacher, Mr Aliyev, was leaving. Nobody knew who started the rumour. Some students said it was true, and they spoke about it in secret during breaks. I decided to ask Mr Aliyev himself. He laughed and said it was a false rumour. He told me a secret instead: he is planning a surprise trip for our class. I promised to keep the secret. It is difficult, but If someone asks me, I will not tell a lie; I will just say I don't know.
